findings.reason: the clause is the part of the fix that stops the next reader chasing a job that never ran, and without a case asserting the refusal text a worker can deliver a green suite that leaves it unimplemented.
findings.text: §26's deliverable requires that "the refusal names which arm and why", but the done-when measures only readability: a no-receipt log and a return-code-disagreeing log must be unreadable, and neither case asserts the refusal identifies the arm or the real reason, so an implementation that widens the receipt search and leaves the existing message ("the measured {name} arm did not run", landing_measure.py:1071-1080) in place passes every case while reporting the wrong reason for an arm that did run

response_events.note: §26's done-when now asserts the refusal text: each unreadable case refuses naming the arm (baseline or after) and its real reason, no receipt or a receipt disagreeing with the return code, never 'did not run' for an arm whose log holds test output.
